subject: ventures/coffee-roaster-margin-calculator
professional: a specialty coffee roastery operations manager / cost accountant; they check first that roast loss is applied as green / (1 - loss) and not green x (1 + loss), then margin vs markup on each channel, then whether wholesale (usually 5 lb bags priced per lb) and retail bags can be costed side by side, then how break-even volume is built

evidence.correctness: Independent exact-fraction Python model (scratchpad/coffee/model.py, written from roasting-cost practice, not from calc.mjs) recomputed every page-default output and calc.mjs matches to the cent: roasted cost 5.10/0.85+0.40+0.10 = $6.50/lb, roast-loss share $0.90; four channels (Online 3.96 / 24.8%, Subscription 2.41 / 16.7%, Wholesale 3.82 / 39.8%, Farmers market 9.71 / 60.7%; profit per roasted lb and per 60 lb roasting hour all match); weekly plan 165 roasted lb, 194.1 green, 7 batches, 2.1 h, 0.5 wk cover, 6 sacks; break-even 618 bags. Blend at target 86 with the page lots: my own 1% grid and a hand LP-vertex analysis (the continuous optimum of a 2-constraint LP mixes two lots) both give 75% Colombia / 25% Ethiopia at $6.441 per roasted lb, score 86, saving $2.03 vs Ethiopia alone ($8.471); calc.mjs returns the same. Roast-loss formula is the correct one. Scored 3 not 4: input handling (craft) can turn a blank or mistyped field into a silent $0.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page feature end to end in node: roast-loss cost, bag economics, channel table with fees and postage, profit per roasted lb and per roasting hour, blend optimizer with share limits and pounds available, cost-of-score frontier, weekly plan, break-even, CSV export, usage counters with opt-out (usage.test.mjs). All work. Gaps: the 'Retail price per bag' input (index.html:61) changes nothing, because parseChannels requires a price on every line so channelTable's discountPct/retailPrice path (calc.mjs:65) is unreachable from the page (retail 16 -> 25 leaves every row identical); priceForMargin exists in calc.mjs but is not on the page. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 31 pass, 0 fail. Eight hand-seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout: caught 3 (roast loss divide->multiply, unweighted blend score, margin on cost instead of revenue); survived 5 (card fee charged on price instead of price+shipping charged; pounds-available check ignoring roast loss; sacks ceil->round; green lb per batch ignoring roast loss; bagsPerWeek 4.345->4). The core happy-path numbers are pinned, but the pounds-available constraint, the sack order and the green weigh-out the page tells the roaster to use are untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (266 lines), index.html script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. calc.mjs is pure, short and readable, no dependencies. Defects: num() falls back to 0 for anything non-numeric and Number('') is 0, so a blank green price gives a $0.50 roasted lb and 'abc' gives $0, and a blank roast loss silently means 0% (calc.mjs:9-12,17,19); European '5,10' becomes $510/lb. parseLots splits on commas, so 'Kenya, 1,200, 88' is accepted as $1/lb, score 200, roast loss 88% with no problem reported, and lots get no range checks at all (calc.mjs:96-111) although roastedCostPerLb rejects loss >= 50%. index.html:174 Number(v('shrink'))||15 turns a typed 0% into 15%. Dead code: discountPct/retailPrice path.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present on index.html (footer), the guide and README; privacy and usage events match usage.mjs (page.test.mjs checks). Guide worked example ($6.00, $6.50, $4.88, $0.76, $9.46 59.1%, $3.96, $3.82) recomputed and matches. FAQ '$5.10 at 15% -> $6.00' matches. FAQ and README say the optimizer checks 'every blend in 5% steps'; with 7-8 coffees it uses 10% steps (calc.mjs:151), shown in the result note but not in the claim. 'Retail price per bag' label implies an input that does something. llms.txt points at duncan-haywood.github.io, but build_pages_site.py rewrite_base_urls rewrites that host at deploy (source-only, not filed); marisstella.app was refused by the session proxy (403), so the served copy was not loaded.
evidence.fitness: Walked a micro-roaster's job: costing a 12 oz retail bag and comparing online, subscription and market works, and the postage insight is real. Wholesale is where it breaks: bag size is one global field (calc.mjs:63), so a 5 lb cafe bag cannot be costed beside 12 oz retail (the test's own 'Cafe 5 lb' channel is priced as a 12 oz bag); there is no price-for-target-margin on the page, so 'what do I charge a cafe for 40% margin' cannot be answered ($9.63 from calc.priceForMargin, hidden); break-even assumes every bag sells at the best channel's profit.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard roastery costing (green / (1 - shrink), margin on revenue, contribution per lb, fixed-cost break-even on a channel mix). Sound: shrink formula, fees on gross including shipping charged, margin on revenue, post-roast blend costing per roasted lb with per-lot loss, green weigh-out. Departures: break-even uses the single best channel's profit per bag (Farmers market $9.71 -> 618 bags/month) rather than a sales mix; at the wholesale $3.82 it would be 1,571, 2.5x more; no per-channel bag size (wholesale per-lb pricing); markup never shown alongside margin; no packing labour per bag or sample/QC loss line (can be folded into packaging by hand).

defects.what: Break-even assumes every bag sells at the single best channel's profit (index.html passes the Farmers market $9.71 bag): 618 bags/month, where a wholesale-heavy roaster needs up to 1,571 (2.5x). No sales-mix input.
num() returns 0 for blank or non-numeric input and Number('') is 0, so a blank or mistyped green price prices coffee at $0, a blank roast loss means 0%; '5,10' becomes $510/lb. No message.
parseLots splits on commas and range-checks nothing: 'Kenya, 1,200, 88' is accepted as $1/lb, cup score 200, roast loss 88%; lot roast loss >= 50% is accepted although roastedCostPerLb rejects it.
One global bag size for every channel, so wholesale 5 lb bags cannot be costed beside 12 oz retail; no price-for-target-margin on the page (priceForMargin exists, unused) and no markup shown.
5 of 8 seeded mutations survive: pounds-available check without roast loss, sacks rounding, green weigh-out per batch, fee on shipping charged, bags per week.
'Retail price per bag' input is dead: every channel line must carry a price, so the discountPct/retailPrice path is unreachable from the page.
FAQ and README say the optimizer checks every blend in 5% steps; with 7-8 coffees it uses 10%.
Number(v('shrink')) || 15 turns a typed 0% roast loss into 15% for blend lots without their own loss.

verdict: Every number recomputed independently (roasted cost, four channels, blend optimum by own grid and LP vertices, weekly plan, break-even) matches calc.mjs, and the roast-loss and margin formulas are the ones a roastery cost accountant uses. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (31 tests pass but 5 of 8 seeded mutations survive, including the pounds-available constraint and the green weigh-out), craft is 2 (blank or mistyped inputs silently become $0 or 0%, lot lines are never range-checked), and fitness and domain are 2 because wholesale cannot be costed in its own bag size, there is no price-for-margin on the page, and break-even assumes every bag sells at the best channel. Finished (completeness 3) at a happy-path level.
